question: If the power of a convex lens is 3 dioptre, then its focal length will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**+0.33 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points:__

__
 
• The given **power **is 3 Dioptre.
 
• **P = 3D.**
 
• We know that the **focal length **is:
 
 
• **f = {1 over power} **
 
 
 
• Therefore, f = {1over 3}
 
• f = 0.333 m
 
• Therefore, the focal length of the 3D power is **+0.33m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The **focal length **of a **convex lens **is defined as the **distance **between the **lens's center **and its **focus**.
 
• The point where light rays **converge parallel **to the main axis is where the real **focus **resides.
 
• In a convex lens, **incident light **constantly moves from **left **to **right **since the object is always on the left side of the lens.
 
• All measures are regarded as **positive **distances when taken from the **right side **of the lens to its **optical center. **
